questions.q: When you describe an agent in natural language on the Copilot Studio Home page, what happens to the AI's suggested triggers, knowledge sources, and tools?
options: They are automatically and permanently added to the agent with no review
They are suggestions only — you review each one and can add, dismiss, or ignore it
They are discarded immediately and never shown to you
They can only be approved by a tenant administrator
questions.explain: Describing an agent generates draft suggestions, but none are permanent until you explicitly review and accept them. They don't persist beyond the current session if ignored.

questions.q: What is the alternative to describing an agent in natural language?
options: There is no alternative — natural language description is required
Selecting Create blank agent, naming it yourself, and configuring everything manually
Importing a .pptx file as the agent's instructions
Copying an agent from another Microsoft 365 tenant
questions.explain: Create blank agent skips the natural-language step: you name the agent yourself and optionally adjust advanced settings like primary language and solution.

questions.q: On an agent's Overview page, what is the maximum length of the Instructions field?
options: 42 characters
1,024 characters
8,000 characters
There is no maximum
questions.explain: The instructions field — the plain-language guidance that shapes how the agent behaves — can hold up to 8,000 characters, far more than the 1,024-character initial description.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend testing a new agent in the test panel BEFORE adding any tools or knowledge sources?
options: Because the test panel stops working once a tool is added
To establish a baseline, so that later, if a response looks wrong, you can tell whether it's the instructions, a missing knowledge source, or a misfiring tool
Because Copilot Studio requires at least one successful test before tools can be added
Because testing with tools attached costs significantly more Copilot credits
questions.explain: Testing with nothing attached shows what the instructions alone produce. That baseline makes it much easier to diagnose problems once tools and knowledge sources are layered on.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT something you configure directly from the agent's Overview page?
options: The agent's instructions
The agent's underlying AI model
Knowledge sources the agent can draw on
A Netlify deployment pipeline for the agent's website
questions.explain: The Overview page covers details, instructions, model selection, knowledge, and triggers/tools — not deployment infrastructure like Netlify, which has nothing to do with Copilot Studio agent configuration.
